build.summary: I built diag-lesion-morphologies. Lesions can now have eccentric (elliptical) lumens whose %DS depends on the view, tapering references, a placement at a side branch, focal spasm that relaxes with the engine's nitrate effect, and thrombus drawn by TIMI thrombus grade (a filling defect with haze, or a convex meniscus at an occlusion). SCAD types 1, 2A, 2B and 3 are drawn too; type 1 has a false lumen that holds contrast. CTOs get a stump shape, an occluded length and explicit collateral channels: the CollateralChannel's Werner grade sets the channel's calibre, speed and filling strength, its Rentrop grade sets how much of the recipient fills, and its tortuosity sets the meander. contrastTransport now times the late retrograde filling through these channels, and the automatic channels of a CTO without its own description use the same transport, so filling looks the same in both labs. projectedStenosis() exports the true %DS per view for QCA and the debrief only. The case generator accepts these morphologies through a new spec option, and a SCAD scenario that names no type takes one from the seed. A new pack adds the seven scenarios, and their events reach the tips. Cases without morphology fields draw exactly as before: on the default path, 103 of 104 existing PCI and library cases give byte-identical trees and scenes (the exception is PCI rca-cto, whose collateral filling is now timed by the new transport). The re-captured baseline set scored 189/236 with no rows lost or gained.

build.notes:
Snapshots of the five existing files and the .started marker are in datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/diag-lesion-morphologies/. coronaryGrowth.ts was not changed: the outward surface normal is taken through samplePos with h + 1 mm, so no growth export was needed.

Design choices:
1. Severity of an eccentric lesion is the %DS along the minor axis (the worst view). The minor axis lies at orientationDeg about the vessel axis, measured from the outward surface normal. tv.radii keeps the equal-area radius for flow and transport.
2. The per-view truth mirrors XrayRenderer's flattened-tube geometry: the 0.2 mm minor semi-axis floor and the blend to a round lumen when the vessel is seen end-on. It uses the central ray in rest geometry.
3. The new thrombus look (defect, haze, meniscus) applies only when the lesion has a thrombusGrade. Without one, morphology 'thrombus' keeps the old stippled look, because PCI lcx-stemi carries morphology 'thrombus' with no grade and pci/scenarios/scenarios.test.ts asserts its tree is unchanged. diag-ohca-post-rosc keeps its look for the same reason.
4. A CTO with morphology 'cto' and a cto object draws the channels it describes. Any other CTO (generated, PCI rca-cto, core graft-search) keeps the automatic channels, now with channel metadata and the shared timing (lag through the channels, then spread through the recipient bed both ways across branch points, with a delayed, dispersed copy of the donor's inlet). The PCI rca-cto filling peaks at about 6 s with a magnitude close to the old model's.
5. Branch lesions are moved so the branch leaves at branchAt; tree.lesionSites records where each lesion was drawn. The engine's flow map still uses the case's unmoved positions, a shift of at most a lesion half-width.
6. CaseSpec.morphology and CaseSpec.eccentric draw details from a separate seeded stream, so specs without them generate identical cases.
7. The pack is diag-eccentric-orthogonal, diag-tapering-reference, diag-lesion-at-branch, diag-cto-contralateral-collaterals (script raises total-occlusion and cto on the first right injection), diag-scad-types (scad-suspected from the start, type by seed), diag-focal-rca-spasm and diag-two-candidate-culprits (thrombus and total-occlusion on the left run). Every value in them is scenario data.

Not built:
- cp-ostial#7 (P3) has no dedicated ostial scenario; catheter-tip spasm belongs to diag-spasm-states.
- The pm-interpreting#5/#6/#11 drills (P2, real-angiogram labelling, Rentrop and Werner answers, culprit naming) are not built. The lesion data and scenarios here give them the virtual lesions and channel grades to score against.

Collateral speeds and gains were tuned in this session so the filling is visible in the live lab within its 6 s contrast window. Final values: CC0/CC1/CC2 at 30/45/60 mm/s with gains 0.25/0.4/0.5, recipient spread 80 mm/s.

Browser hygiene: the rod-mechanics switch to simple was in page memory only (localStorage untouched). The viewport was reset to desktop and tab-21 closed. Browser frames and scratch scripts are in the scratchpad; the capture set dlm-morph is in datasets/tmp/captures and its scorecard in datasets/tmp/realism/reports/dlm-morph.

review.verdict: Accept, with two major follow-ups that sit outside this package's files and a few minor fixes. The design is implemented on the default ribbon path: eccentric elliptical lumens with a per-view truth that matches XrayRenderer's flattened-tube geometry, taper, branch placement with Medina, spasm relief, thrombus by TIMI thrombus grade (filling defect, haze, meniscus), SCAD types 1/2A/2B/3 with a false lumen that holds contrast, CTO stump and length, explicit Werner/Rentrop/tortuosity channels, and lag-based retrograde transport shared with the automatic channels. The caseGenerator option and the seven-scenario pack, picked up by the registry glob, are also in place. The only listed file left unchanged is coronaryGrowth.ts, and the builder explains why. The integrator note is in sceneBuilder next to tubesToSegments. No file under src/ newer than .started lies outside the package list. The default path is unchanged: a lesion with no morphology fields reduces to the old concentric profile value for value, relaxSpasm returns the same array, retroLags exits early, and automatic channels keep 30 mm/s. The only deliberate change is the timing of the automatic CTO collaterals (PCI rca-cto). I ran the package tests (3 files, 26 passed), the regression files (pci/scenarios, diagnosticScenarios/scenarios, caseGenerator, reachability: 45 passed) and tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit (clean, exit 0). The tests are not tautological. They use the real PatientEngine GTN effect, orthogonality-checked C-arm pairs, half-peak timing across 3 seeds of 2 scenarios, and a before/after reachability comparison. The new MORPHOLOGY, COLLATERAL and RETRO values are labelled MODEL PARAMETER, and the Werner, Rentrop, TIMI thrombus grade and SCAD definitions match pci-manual/09-interpreting.ts and complex-pci/12-other-complex.ts. projectedStenosis has no caller outside tests, so no ground truth reaches a live screen. Scenario checks are kept for the debrief only. Spelling is British throughout and I found no American spellings. Per-frame allocations are added only for vessels that carry a shape or retro fill, and follow the existing per-frame tube-building pattern.

findings.where: src/render/xray/coronaryTree.ts lesionGeom, the `l.morphology === "thrombus" && l.thrombusGrade !== undefined` branch (and `MORPHOLOGY.defectHalfLenD[grade] ?? 0.6`)
findings.problem: ThrombusGrade includes 0, meaning no thrombus (caseModel.test.ts uses thrombusGrade: 0). A grade-0 lesion enters the thrombus branch. defectHalfLenD has no key 0, so the `?? 0.6` fallback draws a grade-3-sized filling defect (0.6 D half-length) with haze. The stipple gate in the thrombus.push line also turns off for grade 0.
findings.fix: In lesionGeom, use `else if (l.morphology === "thrombus" && (l.thrombusGrade ?? 0) > 0) {`. That way grade 0 draws neither the defect nor haze, and the existing stipple gate (`thrombusGrade !== undefined`) keeps grade 0 from drawing the stipple either. Drop the dead `l.thrombusGrade ?? 3`. Add a test asserting that thrombusGrade 0 gives no shape.defect or shape.haze.

findings.problem: The haze is a solid tube of radius r*1.35+0.15 with positive iodine laid over the whole lumen. It brightens the opacified lumen itself by up to 12% as well as drawing a halo. The design asks for intraluminal lucency and haze, so the lumen at the thrombus should not get denser.
findings.fix: Make the haze an annulus, the way the calcium shell is built. After pushing the haze tube, push a second tube over the same run with `r: radii.slice(a, z + 1)` and the haze mu negated (`[0, -x[1] * VESSEL_PROFILE.thrombusHaze * sh.haze![a + j], 0]`), so iodine is added only outside the lumen.

fix.notes:
I applied six findings and routed four items that fall outside the package's files: findings 2, 8 and 9, and the FluoroView half of finding 1 (see rejected). The package tests and the typecheck pass.

What changed:
- **Finding 1, interim half (spasm scenario).** I confirmed the problem: nothing outside the scene builder and the tests passes epicardialDilation to the scene. I took diag-focal-rca-spasm out of lesions.launch.ts and out of the exported `scenarios` array in lesions.ts. It now sits in a new `heldScenarios` export with a comment saying why. This removal was needed because scenarios.test.ts requires every scenario in the registry to have a launch entry, so the practice index, the registry and the case library no longer offer it. The morphology tests still build it through scenarioCase's lookup argument. lesions.test.ts now checks that it is held back, absent from the registry and still drawn. If diag-spasm-states publishes diag-focal-rca-spasm, as its plan says, it should move the `heldScenarios` entry into spasm.ts rather than define it again; otherwise the id is duplicated.
- **Finding 3 (thrombus grade 0).** In coronaryTree.ts lesionGeom the branch is now `(l.thrombusGrade ?? 0) > 0`. I removed the dead `?? 3` and changed the fallback to `defectHalfLenD[grade] ?? 0`. New test: grade 0 gives no defect, no haze, no stipple and no negative-iodine tubes.
- **Finding 4 (haze).** The haze in sceneBuilder.ts is now an annulus: the halo tube, plus a tube the size of the lumen with the haze iodine negated. The lumen at the thrombus is no longer denser. The existing defect test now expects two negative tubes, the defect and the haze's inner wall. New test: the inner wall matches the lumen radius and cancels the halo's iodine exactly.
- **Finding 5 (two-candidate CTO tips).** The right-run in diag-two-candidate-culprits now raises cto as well as total-occlusion. src/ui/sim/modules/lesions.test.ts now films a right run after the left one and expects both triggers, the cto event and the tip diag-cto-strategy-defer-adhoc.
- **Finding 6 (FLAP_MM).** Deleted; sceneBuilder.ts imports MORPHOLOGY and uses MORPHOLOGY.flapMm.
- **Finding 7 (calcium shell).** Building the shell on the shifted points, as the review suggested, would not have been enough. On the non-dense path the shell was already on the shifted points (basePts is pts). Even there, its inner radius was the round equal-area radius plus 0.25, which is smaller than the major semi-axis: about 1.07 mm against 0.92 mm for diag-eccentric-orthogonal. So the lumen could still show through. I made three changes:
  - The eccentric geometry is now computed before the contrast block, so the shell is the same with or without contrast.
  - The shell follows the shifted lumen on both paths. On the dense path, each base sample takes the shift of its nearest dense sample.
  - The shell's inner radius is at least the major semi-axis.
